Whole front/reverse Mini images show an exterior rope arch with a visible tied joining region. They do not expose concealed continuation.
Whole Mini side image shows two longitudinal side groove tracks and a transverse midheight track; one exposed lead descends a longitudinal track and turns toward the dark other-track opening.
The retained context photo shows the board against rock, not a hand using the jug or a loaded opening-up pose.
exactCurrentRepresentation: nature_jug binds only FinalSolid.Face6. Its actual exported node is a single-depth recess back plane, not the top rim or an upper-edge pressure surface.
The -90 degree model-X jug-open-up pose rotates that plane into an upward-facing floor. That proves orientation of the authored selection, not identification of the maker jug.

Two 110 mm lead estimates connect to the same invisible metadata anchor. Each ends at its front-track station; a separate 12.5 mm exterior cross segment stops at the rear-track station. The 40 mm value is allowance, not rendered segment length.

The opening-up cache takes the left lead over former lower/front corner and the right lead over former upper/front corner. Their first local points have opposite height signs. The source whole photos do not demonstrate this bearing setup.

nativeGuideCompatibilityAndBoundedPropos.mode: read-only compatibility assessment; no implementation or solve authorized
existingReuse: native_cord_features.extract_native_cord_features accepts groove_names with an empty bore_names list. The six existing Part::Cylinder tools can be selected as grooves without inventing holes.

The extractor derives finite axialBounds from actual matched final-body cylindrical wall faces, with geometry-only bounds. Cutter heights include extension beyond the board and are not substitute terminal stations.
export_rope_collision_solid.py already calls that extractor when either groove names or bore names are selected.
native_cord_guides.certify_groove_traversal proves finite inner traversal; actual material reaction and continuous full-radius collision gates remain useful without a bore.
native_cord_routes already has native segment route solving for both exact terminals; this is reusable for the two transverse segments without converting them to leads.

actualCurrentBlockers.fact: grooveGuides accepts only independent anchor-plane leads; requires every strand in each pose and exact feature/boreFeature/exitSign keys plus mouthAxis.
validate_guide_bindings requires each groove selection to name a separate native bore with actual wallFaces.
certify_bore_entry checks a finite inset and approach into a bore mouth; Mini has only the open transverse groove, so a fake boreFeature would misstate geometry.
lead optimization requires a mouth axis. A guide-only path needs a sourced groove approach/traversal condition, rather than asserting a bore-entry direction.

guided solver treats every strand as an anchor-to-first-terminal lead and uses all rest lengths for initial height. Mini has two leads and two segments, whose second terminal and feasibility-only allowance must stay distinct.

smallestProposedExtensionNotImplemented: Add an explicit source-bound guide-only selection, making boreFeature/bore-entry certification conditional. Select the existing vertical and transverse open grooves as their actual kind; do not rename a transverse groove as a bore.
Allow a lead subset for guide optimization and lead-driven settling; keep segment routes on existing native two-terminal solving, with segment lengths as feasibility allowances.

For guide-only leads retain finite axial/radial traversal and correct sourced exit/approach direction, actual-material reaction gates, and continuous rounded-cache signed-solid/interstrand full-radius checks.

Bind all selected cutters and derived wall/axial witnesses to the final source hash and each canonical pose. Preserve exact native terminal evidence; do not introduce route waypoints, collars, hidden passages, station nudges, new radii or relaxed tolerances.
